niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Good question — “shadow work” and spiritual practice overlap a lot, but they’re different skills. Shadow work is typically psychological (exploring disowned parts of the self) while spiritual practice gives you steadying resources (meditation, somatic grounding, nonduality, devotional practice). Below are reputable, practical online options organized by type, with quick notes on who they suit and safety tips.

Shadow-work–focused options
- Jung Platform (subscription): a reliable, curated source of courses and talks from Jungian analysts and teachers on the shadow, dreams, archetypes, and integration. Good if you want depth in Jungian theory and applied exercises.
- Internal Family Systems (IFS) — IFS Institute / introductory courses: evidence-based parts work that maps well onto shadow integration. The IFS Institute runs trainings and many teachers offer online intro workshops. Best if you want a structured therapeutic method with clear tools.
- Sounds True / teacher courses (James Hollis, Marianne Williamson, others): hosts lectures/workshops on shadow topics from well-known clinicians and spiritual teachers. Good for lecture-based learning and experiential programs.
- Udemy / Skillshare — shadow-work courses: many affordable, self-paced options (quality varies considerably). Look for high ratings, clear curricula, and teachers with clinical/therapeutic credentials if you want deeper work.

Spiritual-practice (meditation, mindfulness, nonduality, contemplative)
- Palouse Mindfulness (free MBSR-style online course): a complete, teacher-guided MBSR-style program you can do at your own pace. Excellent foundational mindfulness training.
- Waking Up (Sam Harris, app + course content): secular meditation instruction with philosophical context; accessible daily lessons and multi-week courses.
- 10% Happier (app + courses): practical, secular, trauma-aware meditation training and short programs; good for skeptical beginners.
- Insight Timer: thousands of free guided meditations plus paid multi-week courses from teachers worldwide. Good variety and many free community offerings.
- Sounds True / SpiritRock / Spirit Rock teachers (Jack Kornfield, Tara Brach, Pema Chödrön recordings): for compassion practice, RAIN (Tara Brach), and deeper Buddhist-informed shadow work.
- Nonduality/Advaita teachers (Rupert Spira, Adyashanti, Mooji—note: varying approaches): deep inquiry practices for people oriented to direct path spirituality; best if you already have some contemplative experience.

Therapeutic and somatic complements (highly recommended)
- IFS (again) — excellent for inner-part integration.
- Somatic practices: somatic-experiencing intro materials, trauma-informed yoga, or body-centered therapy courses. These are helpful because shadow work can mobilize intense somatic responses.
- Trauma-aware mindfulness/therapy trainings: if you have trauma history, take trauma-informed courses or work with a therapist before doing intensive shadow work.

Where to start (recommended short path)
1. Build a steady grounding practice (daily meditation, breath, body awareness) — try Palouse Mindfulness, Waking Up, or 10% Happier.
2. Learn an integration method — take an introductory IFS course or a Jung-based course from Jung Platform or Sounds True.
3. Do weekly reflective practices: journaling prompts, RAIN (Tara Brach), dream work, creative expression.
4. Add somatic support and, if material becomes intense, a therapist or clinician trained in IFS/trauma work.

Safety & selection tips
- Shadow work can surface strong emotions, memories, and body sensations. Don’t do intensive programs alone if you have complex trauma or active mental-health issues — work with a licensed therapist.
- Prefer teachers with clinical/therapeutic credentials for deep psychological work.
- Read reviews and sample lessons where available. Free introductory material (apps, Insight Timer, Palouse) is a low-risk place to begin.
- Avoid teachers or communities that demand absolute devotion, isolation from other treatment, or expensive upsells with pressure.

If you tell me your background and goals (e.g., trauma history vs. personal growth, more psychological vs. mystical interest, budget, how much time per week), I can recommend 2–3 specific courses/programs tailored to you. Would you like that?
